title: Set up physical constants and interatomic parameters
action: Define all required physical constants and interatomic interaction parameters: cubic half-edge l=2 Å; interaction exponents s=9, t=6; effective Ti charge n=2.06 e; overlap (λ) and van der Waals (μ) coefficients for the ion pairs O–Ti, O–O, Ba–O, Ba–Ba, Ba–Ti, Ti–Ti as listed in the background section; dipolar field coefficients p=8.668, q=30.081; and ionic polarizabilities 4παTi=0.0365(2l)³, 4παBa=0.382(2l)³, 4παO=0.470(2l)³.

title: Derive Ti on-site potential coefficients a and b
action: Using the overlap and van der Waals energy expressions for the tetragonal lattice under the nearest-neighbor approximation, derive the quadratic coefficient a(Δa, Δb1, Δb2) and quartic coefficient b(Δa, Δb1, Δb2) of the Ti on‑site potential. Expand the interatomic energy derivatives around the cubic reference to first order in the deformation ratios, and store the resulting functional forms for later use in the energy minimization.

title: Compute Coulomb energy derivatives
action: Approximate the Coulomb energy of the tetragonal lattice by averaging the Madelung energies of three cubic lattices corresponding to the three cell edges, and differentiate to obtain the linearized derivatives ∂UCoulomb/∂Δa, ∂UCoulomb/∂Δb1, ∂UCoulomb/∂Δb2. Use the Madelung constant −49.1e²/R with R=2l=4 Å for the cubic lattice.

title: Solve local‑field equations and obtain dipole interaction coefficient a′
action: Set up the Slater‑style 5×5 linear equations for the induced dipole moments u (Ti), v (Ba), w (Oa), x₁ (Ob₁), x₂ (Ob₂) using the tetragonal‑modified dipolar field coefficients that include nearest‑neighbor corrections proportional to Δa. Insert the provided ionic polarizabilities and solve the system numerically to express each induced dipole as a linear function of the bare Ti‑site dipole u₀ and Δa. From the solution for the Ti induced dipole, derive the dipole‑energy contribution a′(Δa) = a₀′(1 − 7.30 Δa), where a₀′ = 0.1974·(ne)²/(2αTi). Store a₀′ and the sensitivity factor 7.30 for the minimization step.

title: Solve equilibrium equations and compute lattice deformation and Ti shift
action: Combine the energy gradients from overlap, van der Waals, Coulomb, and dipole terms to form the two coupled equilibrium equations ∂U/∂Δa = 0 and ∂U/∂Δb = 0, setting Δb1 = Δb2 = Δb. Solve the resulting nonlinear system numerically for Δa and Δb. Then compute the Ti ion displacement x = sqrt(−(a′ + a)/(2b)) using the converged values of a, b, and a′. Write the results to /app/outputs/lattice_deformation.json containing the three scalar values.
description: Spontaneous lattice deformation ratios and Ti ion displacement for effective Ti charge n=2.06 e.
